subtopic: Nutrition and mood in general terms
passage: I'm Devika, and my brother Chinmay is eight. At Tanya's birthday party he had two pieces of cake, a fistful of toffees and a fizzy drink. For an hour he was everywhere, jumping off the sofa arms, shouting, spinning till he fell over. Then, around six, it was like someone had pulled his plug. He sat in a corner rubbing his eyes, and cried when I said it was time to go. At home he snapped at Mummy about his shoes. I don't really know what was going on inside him. Mummy didn't lecture or ban sweets. Before the next party she gave him a proper dal-rice lunch, and there he had one piece of cake. He was still bouncy, but there was no crying in corners.

qa.q: What did Chinmay have at Tanya's party?
qa.a: Chinmay had two pieces of cake, a fistful of toffees and a fizzy drink.

qa.q: What might Chinmay's crying in the corner suggest?
qa.a: It suggests Chinmay was tired and cranky after the burst of energy, though Devika could not know for sure.

qa.q: What did Mummy change for the next party, and why is it wiser than a ban?
qa.a: Mummy gave Chinmay a proper lunch first and he had one piece of cake, which kept his mood steadier without making sweets forbidden.

qa.q: What was the party like for Devika to watch?
qa.a: Devika watched Chinmay go from spinning everywhere to crying in a corner, and seemed puzzled by the sudden change.

grounding: A child after lots of sweets seems hyper, then tired and irritable, and a proper meal with a treat in moderation keeps his mood steadier.

subtopic: Nutrition and mood in general terms
passage:
Week one. Every day Pradeep's tiffin held sweet biscuits and a packet of jelly sweets. By eleven he was drumming on the desk and chatting nonstop. By twelve he was yawning, head on his arms, snapping at anyone who spoke to him. Zainab Ma'am noticed the pattern.
Week two. She mentioned it gently to his father at pickup, without blame. "Nothing needs banning," she said. "Maybe something filling alongside?" His father nodded; he had noticed the evening grumps too.
Week four. Pradeep's tiffin now held a paratha with paneer, some fruit and one biscuit as a treat. At twelve he was still upright, finishing his sums, and he laughed when he got one wrong instead of throwing his pencil.

qa.q: What was in Pradeep's tiffin in week four?
qa.a: A paratha with paneer, some fruit and one biscuit as a treat.

qa.q: How was Pradeep feeling by twelve in week one?
qa.a: Pradeep felt tired and irritable, yawning with his head on his arms and snapping at others.

qa.q: Why was Zainab Ma'am's suggestion helpful?
qa.a: She suggested adding something filling without banning anything, so Pradeep's father could change the tiffin without feeling blamed.

qa.q: What had Pradeep's father noticed at home?
qa.a: Pradeep's father had noticed the evening grumps too.

grounding: A child's energy spikes and crashes after sweets, and a more balanced tiffin with one treat keeps his mood steadier.
